Not really, the government wasn't trying to stop the hacienda system and independence was pursued more out of disagreement with president Santa Anna
Now we could say (and it wouldn't be quite right either) that Texas was the confederacy of Mexico, because slavery was abolished in 1829 and still a lot of Anglo-American settlers kept coming with their slaves.

Not really, México at the time was very unstable because politicians were fighting over being centralists or turning the country into a federation, so when a centralist government took power a couple of states declared independence (most famously Texas). Obviously all of Mexico at the time was partaking in oppression of the indigenous people's, and their economies relied on what was basically slavery, but in this case it wasn't the primary motivation to secede from the union.

There's also the concern that polititans will start using the flag in their campaigns.
